bottom_line.paragraph: The asking price of $589,900 sits in the upper part of what recent sales support. It's inside the range, but it isn't a bargain. The two sales that support this price closed before July, when mortgage rates were lower and homes were selling faster. The summer sales and this home's own price cuts point toward the middle of the range.

offer_plan.intro: Our recommendation for your offer, based on the comparable sales, the market, and this home's history. These three numbers are a negotiating plan, not a value opinion, so we'll adjust them together if anything changes.
offer_plan.why_opening: The bottom of the supported range, backed by the comps. After {active_days} and {price_cuts}, the seller has reason to counter rather than ignore it.
offer_plan.why_target: Where the summer sales and the typical 4% negotiation suggest this home settles.
offer_plan.why_walk_away: Just under the median of the adjusted comps. Above it you'd be paying spring prices and risking a low appraisal you'd have to cover in cash.
offer_plan.conditions: the new roof is permitted and passed its final inspection, the inspection finds nothing major in the 1998 systems, and no other offers are competing. If any of those changes, we'll revisit the numbers before you sign.

offer.heading: Negotiating Points
bullets: There is room to negotiate. The price has come down four times since May, and no buyer has gone under contract at any of those prices. Mortgage rates are also higher now than when the spring sales happened.

Seller help with closing costs is normal right now. Three of every four sales nearby since July included seller-paid costs, typically around $9,500. Asking for a credit instead of a lower price can reduce the cash you need at closing.

Watch the appraisal. Only two similar pool homes nearby have sold above $595,000, both before July. An offer near the top of the range raises the chance the appraisal comes in low, which you would have to cover in cash or renegotiate.

comps.intro: We looked at every sale within one mile since April 2026 and chose the five closest matches: Cattail Crossing pool homes of about 2,200–2,300 square feet, built in the late 1990s. We included the ones that argue against a lower price. For each sale, we adjust for differences so it reflects what that home would have sold for if it were this one.
comps.method_note: Adjustments used: about $75 per square foot of size difference; $30,000–$45,000 for a home that hadn't been updated to this level; $5,000 for documented recent systems this home can't yet match; $10,000 for a pond lot; about 1.5% off spring sales because prices have softened since. Seller-paid costs are subtracted from the sale price, since they reduce what the seller actually received. Condition adjustments are based on listing descriptions, not visits, so they are judgment calls.

comps.summary_paragraph: The adjusted values run from about $572,000 to $595,000, with a median of {median_adjusted}. We lean toward the middle because the two highest sales are strong condition matches but come from a stronger market, while the most recent sales needed the smallest market adjustments and sit lower. Other Cattail Crossing sales support the same picture: 1409 Arrowroot Way (updated, pool) sold for $566,000 in May, and 1586 Buttonbush Dr (renovated, no pool) sold for $552,000 in June.

market.intro: We looked at 38 sales within one mile of this home between April and mid-September 2026. The market has cooled noticeably since spring.
rows: Typical Sale vs. Original Asking Price
Typical Days to Go Under Contract
bullets: Homes are selling for about 4% under their original asking price, after seller-paid costs, compared with about 1% in the spring. Sellers are now expecting to negotiate.

Inventory is balanced. There are 15 other homes for sale in this area, and at the summer pace of sales that's about three months of supply. That's neither a buyer's market nor a seller's market, but it has shifted toward buyers. Two in three current listings have already cut their price.

Mortgage rates are up. The national average 30-year rate was 6.95% the week of September 17, versus roughly 6.2–6.4% during the spring sales. That's the main reason the spring prices are harder to repeat now.

Price per square foot. Cattail Crossing homes have sold for a median of about $243 per square foot since April. This home is asking $266. That's supportable for an updated pool home with a new roof, but only two similar sales have been higher.

taxes.heading: Property taxes will be much higher than the listing shows
taxes.intro: The listing shows $5,212 in taxes. That's the 2025 bill, based on the current owner's capped assessment and homestead exemption. In Florida, a home's taxable value is reset when it sells, so your bill will be based on roughly what you pay. You also get to file for your own homestead exemption.
taxes.note: Based on 2025 final millage rates (13.6790 unincorporated; 16.7784 City of Oviedo). We still need to confirm which applies; the property appraiser's record shows it. These estimates assume the county values the home at the purchase price, and it often values homes somewhat lower, so treat these as the high end. Garbage and other flat assessments aren't included. File for homestead by March 1 of the year after you close.
taxes.after_paragraph: Your first year matters. Your lender will likely set up your escrow using the seller's lower bill. When your own higher bill arrives, your monthly payment can rise to cover the difference. Budget for the higher number from the start.

insurance.paragraph: The main things that drive the cost for this house are the new roof (insurers will want its permit date), the 1998 AC and water heater if they're original, wind-mitigation features, and the pool. The flood zone (X) is outside the high-risk area, but Citizens requires flood coverage on many policies (and on every Citizens policy from January 2027), so get a flood quote with the homeowners quote. Get a real quote during your inspection period, after the 4-point and wind-mitigation inspections. The payment estimates below use $4,200 a year as a placeholder, not a quote.

payment.intro: Three common ways to finance this home at the target price. Your lender will give you exact numbers.

credit_scenarios.intro: The seller cares about what they net; you may care more about the cash you need at closing. These three offers have about the same price minus credit but split it differently between price and a credit toward your closing costs.
credit_scenarios.after_paragraph: Each $5,000 of credit saves you about {credit_cash_per_5k} at closing and costs about {credit_monthly_per_5k} a month. That's worth it if cash is tight or you might sell within a decade, and less so if you have savings to spare and plan to stay long term. All three prices sit below the median adjusted comp, so the appraisal should support any of them.

items: The new roof. The listing says the roof was replaced this summer, while the home was off the market. Roof age is the biggest factor in insuring a Florida home, so we want the permit, the final inspection and any warranty in writing.
Why the price keeps coming down. Four cuts in four months can simply mean an ambitious first price, but ask whether any buyer's inspection or feedback raised a problem.
1998 systems. Neither the AC's nor the water heater's age is listed. If they're original, they're near the end of their life, and insurers ask about both.
Permits for the remodel. Confirm the kitchen, bath, and any plumbing or electrical work was permitted. Unpermitted work can cause problems with insurance and future resale.
The third bath. Check that the property appraiser's record shows three full baths, and if one was added, confirm it was permitted.
Pool equipment and screen enclosure. Neither age is listed. Also confirm the pool has a compliant safety barrier.

"As-Is" doesn't mean no inspection. If the offer is written on the As-Is contract, you still get an inspection period in which you can cancel for any reason. It only means the seller isn't committing to repairs.
questions: Can you share the roof permit, the final inspection, and any roofer's warranty? Is there a new wind-mitigation report?

How old are the AC, water heater, and pool equipment?
Were the kitchen, bathroom, and any electrical or plumbing updates permitted?
Is the third full bath original to the house?
Is the seller open to contributing toward the buyer's closing costs?

method: This analysis uses the Stellar MLS listing and full price history for 1438 Buttonbush Dr, a Stellar MLS search of single-family homes within one mile (sales from April 6 to September 15, 2026, plus current active, pending, and expired listings), Seminole County Property Appraiser 2025 final millage rates, and the Freddie Mac weekly mortgage rate survey for September 17, 2026.

This is a broker's opinion of value based on comparable sales. It is not an appraisal. A lender's appraiser works under different standards and may reach a different number. Tax, insurance, and payment figures are estimates for planning, not quotes, so confirm them with your lender and insurance agent. Market conditions change, so this analysis should be refreshed if you haven't made an offer within a few weeks.
